# Scud 3.0.0 — focused task workflows and stateless MCP

Scud now focuses on PRD-to-task proposals, safe task-list ingestion and updates,
and dependency-aware live status for scripted workflows. sb remains optional;
ensemble inference is explicitly experimental.

## Breaking changes and migration

- **Smaller command/API surface.** Coding-agent execution, swarm, commit and
  the former utility commands are no longer registered. Use `scud --help` for
  the supported surface. Old source packages remain pending staged cleanup;
  they are not an exposed compatibility API.
- **New task store:** `.scud/tasks/tasks.json`. Nonempty legacy
  `.scud/tasks/tasks.scg` files are refused, not silently imported or modified.
  Keep an exact backup and review conversion to the versioned JSON document
  before archiving the old file. A safe automated legacy converter is still
  follow-up work. Do not mix old SCG-writing binaries with this store.
- **Main and fast models**, selected through `scud models list`,
  `scud models set main QUERY`, and `scud models set fast QUERY`. No task-role,
  tier or complexity-based routing in the core path. Fresh projects have no
  implicit model default. Configure provider credentials in the documented
  environment variables; foreign application credential files are not scraped.
- **Stateless MCP 2026-07-28 only.** Update clients to send protocol version
  and client capabilities in every request's `params._meta`. There is no
  initialize/initialized handshake, persistent HTTP session ID or legacy GET/SSE
  session stream. The official Go SDK version is v1.8.0; SDK and protocol
  generation numbers are separate.
- Building from source requires **Go 1.27.3** or newer.

## New workflow

```sh
scud init
scud models list
scud models set main 'a uniquely matching model name'
scud models set fast 'another uniquely matching model name'
scud parse product.md > tasks.json
scud validate --input tasks.json
scud import tasks.json
scud status --watch --interval 500ms
```

Task commands emit JSON by default. Imports and patches use strict decoding,
full-graph validation, process-safe locking, atomic publication and optional
revision guards. Cross-phase/parent dependencies determine readiness.
Filtered document exports include prerequisite phases. Workflow status is
user-reported and is not a verification certificate.

## MCP and sb

```sh
scud mcp-server
scud mcp-server --transport http --listen 127.0.0.1:8080
scud sb check --json
```

Five core MCP tools plus opt-in sb, with stdio and loopback Streamable HTTP.
Raw transport validation rejects duplicate JSON keys and preserves large
integer values. EOF/disconnect cancels active work. HTTP validates version,
method and tool-name headers, rejects cross-origin browser requests, and
creates no persistent session.

Passing sb gates may produce no discharge report. Present/changed reports
remain labelled unverified; scud never silently changes task status from them.
Linux/macOS supervise the private invocation process group through launcher
exit. Windows/other-platform cleanup currently covers the direct child only;
detached process groups are outside Unix ownership. Windows console input is
rejected where it cannot be interrupted safely; scripted pipes are supported.

## Reliability

Three independent SME-style reviews identified ten issues, all addressed with
regressions: exact provider/model identity, multiline TOML preservation,
transitive deterministic sorting, standalone exports, no-op revision stability,
subprocess ownership, blocked-input cancellation, catalog error identity, raw
MCP ingestion and disconnect cleanup. A follow-up review confirmed per-request
metadata enforcement cannot fall back to prior connection state.

Build, tests, race checks, vet and Windows cross-compilation passed locally.
Provider behavior is fixture-tested, not a promise of live account access or
support for every model exposed by a provider catalog.
